plain.text: Two years later, Pharaoh had two dreams. In the first, seven fat cows came up from the Nile, then seven ugly, thin cows came up and ate them. In the second, seven healthy heads of grain were swallowed up by seven thin, scorched heads. Pharaoh was troubled, but none of his magicians or wise men could interpret the dreams. Then the chief cupbearer remembered Joseph and told Pharaoh about the young Hebrew in prison who had interpreted their dreams correctly.

Pharaoh sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought from the dungeon. Pharaoh said he had heard Joseph could interpret dreams. Joseph replied, "I cannot do it, but God will give Pharaoh the answer he desires." Pharaoh told his dreams. Joseph said both dreams meant the same thing: God was showing Pharaoh what he was about to do. Seven years of great abundance would come, followed by seven years of severe famine. The dream was given twice because the matter was firmly decided by God and would happen soon. Joseph advised Pharaoh to appoint a wise man to collect a fifth of the harvest during the good years and store it for the famine.

Pharaoh and his officials liked the plan. Pharaoh said, "Can we find anyone like this man, in whom is the Spirit of God?" He put Joseph in charge of all Egypt, second only to Pharaoh himself. He gave him his signet ring, fine linen robes and a gold chain, and had him ride in a chariot as people shouted, "Bow down!" He gave him an Egyptian name and a wife, Asenath.

Joseph was thirty years old when he entered Pharaoh's service. During the seven good years he stored huge amounts of grain in the cities, so much that they stopped counting. Joseph had two sons. He named the firstborn Manasseh, saying, "God has made me forget all my hardship." He named the second Ephraim, saying, "God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction."

The seven years of plenty ended and the famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in every land, but in Egypt there was food. When the Egyptians cried out to Pharaoh, he said, "Go to Joseph and do what he tells you." Joseph opened the storehouses and sold grain. People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, because the famine was severe everywhere.

summary.bigIdea: God gives Joseph wisdom to interpret Pharaoh's dreams, and Joseph rises from prison to rule Egypt and save many lives.
points: Pharaoh dreams of seven fat and seven thin cows; Joseph says, "God will give Pharaoh a sound answer."
Joseph is made ruler over Egypt and stores grain during seven good years.
When famine comes, the whole world comes to Joseph for food.
summary.reflection: Joseph named his son Ephraim: "God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction." Where might God bring fruit from your hard times?
